title: Food, water, heat become mind, breath, speech (6.5)
hook: the father tells his son to stop eating for fifteen days, then asks him to recite the Vedas
carry: you are what you eat, literally
tomorrow: sleep: the bird returns to the tree

segments.voice: Yesterday: trivrit, red for heat, white for water, black for food. Your line was behind the colors. What did you see something made of? Today ends week two of year two. Day three hundred forty-three.

Four o'clock, and no lunch. The same email, read three times, and it still won't go in. A short temper, a foggy head. Then someone hands over a sandwich, and ten minutes later the email makes sense. That's usually filed under being hungry, not under the nature of the mind. Uddalaka files it under the mind. He even turns it into a test, with his own son as the subject.
screen: `FOUR O'CLOCK, NO LUNCH.` → `THE SAME EMAIL, THREE TIMES.` → `A SANDWICH, AND YOU'RE BACK.`

segments.voice: Uddalaka tells his son what happens to the three stuffs once they're inside you. Food, when eaten, divides into three. The coarsest part leaves the body. The middle part becomes flesh. The finest part becomes mind. Water, when drunk, divides the same way. The coarsest part leaves. The middle becomes blood. The finest becomes breath. Heat, when taken in, through oils and ghee, divides too. The coarsest becomes bone. The middle becomes marrow. The finest becomes speech. So mind is made of food, breath of water, speech of heat. Shvetaketu says, please, tell me more. So his father gives him an experiment. Don't eat for fifteen days. Drink water as you like, since breath is made of water and you'll need it. Shvetaketu fasts. Then he comes back, and his father says: recite the Vedas. And he can't. Nothing comes, sir. His father gives a picture: when a great fire has burned down to one ember the size of a firefly, it can't burn much. But add straw, and it blazes again. Go eat. Shvetaketu eats, comes back, and now he can answer every question. The mind is made of food, my dear. Seven days this week, in one breath. Upakosala and the fires. The king's five fires. The proud son and the one question. The clay. Being alone, which thought, let me be many. The three colors. And today: food becoming mind. The Chandogya keeps refusing to separate the sacred from the stomach.
screen: `FOOD BECOMES FLESH AND MIND.` · `WATER, BREATH. HEAT, SPEECH.` · `FIFTEEN DAYS WITHOUT FOOD.` · `THE EMBER AND THE STRAW.` · then, large: `THE MIND IS MADE OF FOOD.`

segments.voice: Today's practice notices the ember. Sit and settle. Notice how your body feels right now: hungry, full, somewhere between. Notice your mind's brightness: sharp, foggy, tired. Without judging either, just see how they go together. Then think of the last thing you ate, and where it came from, and that some of it is now the attention you're paying to this moment. Breathe with that. The bell holds the time.
Food. In Uddalaka's lesson, the finest part of food becomes mind, as the finest part of water becomes breath, and of heat, speech.
Your line: you are what you eat, literally. Today, notice the hour your focus dips, and check when you last ate. Day three hundred forty-three.

screen: `DAY 343 COUNTS.` → `WEEK TWO OF YEAR TWO, DONE.` → `TOMORROW: SLEEP.`

howItsDone: In Hindu homes food is often offered to God before it is eaten, and traditions of mindful eating and dietary practice connect what one eats with the clarity of the mind.

after fifteen days without food, he can't recite the Vedas

the finest part of food becomes flesh
the middle part becomes flesh; the finest becomes mind.

fork.setup: you're Shvetaketu. you've fasted for fifteen days. your father asks you to recite the Vedas you spent twelve years memorizing. what happens?
fork.reveal: he can't remember. his father compares him to an ember the size of a firefly. after he eats, it all comes back: the mind is made of food.

original.note: Sanskrit manas: mind. annamayaṃ hi somya manaḥ: for the mind, my dear, is made of food.

trapdoor: what you thought: a diet slogan.
what it means: food, water and heat each divide in three inside you; the finest parts become mind, breath and speech.
what a scholar hears: Chandogya 6.5–6.7, with Shvetaketu's fifteen-day fast as a test; annamaya, made of food, is also a word the Taittiriya Upanishad uses for the body's outer layer.
recall: God's gift of love and help, freely given

notes: Editor review (2026-10-01): hook rewritten (opened 'You know the version of yourself', told the listener what they feel, 'everyone/most of us', and an unsourced 'first recorded experiment' claim); week look-back wording varied from day 336; carry practice changed so it no longer repeats day 338's think-of-the-meal carry.
Week end (days 337–343): look-back in the teach.
6.5: food → feces/flesh/mind; water → urine/blood/breath; heat (taken as oil, ghee etc.) → bone/marrow/speech. 'Leaves the body' used for feces/urine; confirm.
The fast and the ember are in 6.7, not 6.5 as the index title gives; the script includes them because they complete the lesson. Confirm.
Hook calls it possibly 'the first recorded experiment in the Upanishads': softened with 'may be'; consider cutting if a Keeper objects.
